title: Tight length bound for processing a nonempty clause against a nonempty path
statement:
Run the clause-processing procedure on a nonempty list of free literals — each paired with its position index in the clause — and a nonempty canonical path, starting from restrictions $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$, and let its output consist of a remaining path and a list of accumulated auxiliary entries (among the updated restrictions). Writing $a$ for the number of auxiliary entries produced, $r$ for the length of the remaining path returned, and $m$ for the length of the input path, we have
\[
a + 1 + 2r \le 2m.
\]
hypotheses_covered: input literal list is nonempty (a head literal-with-index followed by a tail)
input path is nonempty (a head step followed by a tail)
two restrictions ρ₀ and σ are supplied as starting states
replaced:
On non-empty literal and path lists, \texttt{SwitchingLemma2.processClauseLits} satisfies
the strengthened bound: the auxiliary-entry length plus one, plus twice the remaining
path length, is still at most twice the length of the input path.
